title: Angular webapp login loop — isAuthenticated() reads HttpOnly byd_session cookie
description: After fixing the zone.js blank-render (BladeWatch-0u0t), the hosted Angular SPA (web/) renders but traps the user in a /login redirect loop when accessed via browser/zrok tunnel. Root cause: web/src/app/core/auth/auth.service.ts isAuthenticated() decides login state by reading the 'byd_session' cookie from document.cookie — but the server sets byd_session as HttpOnly (AuthApiHandler.handleTokenValidation buildCookie httpOnly=true), so JavaScript can NEVER read it. isAuthenticated() therefore always returns false; authGuard (web/src/app/core/auth/auth.guard.ts) redirects every protected route back to /login even immediately after a successful login (the login component shows 'Login successful! Redirecting...' then bounces back). The server also sets a non-HttpOnly hint cookie byd_auth=1 (httpOnly=false) with the same lifetime, set by BOTH the REST /auth/token path and the Connect AuthService.Login path (captureWithCookies reuses handleTokenValidation). Fix: change isAuthenticated() to test for a non-empty byd_auth cookie instead of byd_session; also clear byd_auth locally in clearAndRedirect() so logout flips state immediately. Verified the loop with a headless Chromium probe over the tunnel: final URL stays /login, app-login stays mounted, visible text 'Login successful! Redirecting...'. Acceptance: after fix + rebuild, headless probe completing the login reaches a non-/login route with a page component (e.g. app-dashboard/app-surveillance) mounted; logout returns to /login. Do not make mistakes.
close_reason: Fixed and verified on device 192.168.1.187 over zrok tunnel via headless Chromium probe: zone.js import added to web/src/main.ts (NG0908 gone, app renders); isAuthenticated() now reads byd_auth hint cookie (login reaches dashboard, no loop). All routes render real content.

title: Angular webapp renders blank — zone.js polyfill never loaded (NG0908)
description: The hosted Angular SPA (web/, Vite + @analogjs/vite-plugin-angular, Angular 19.2.25) renders a blank page everywhere (localhost 127.0.0.1:8080 AND zrok tunnel). Root cause: bootstrap throws NG0908 in the NgZone constructor because zone.js is never loaded. app.config.ts uses provideZoneChangeDetection({eventCoalescing:true}) which REQUIRES zone.js, and zone.js@~0.15.0 is a dependency, but unlike an Angular CLI build the Vite/Analog build does NOT auto-inject zone.js — and web/src/main.ts does not 'import zone.js'. Result: no polyfills chunk in web/dist/assets, Zone global undefined, NgZone ctor throws, <app-root> stays empty. Fix: add "import 'zone.js';" as the FIRST line of web/src/main.ts, rebuild (npm run build copies web/dist into app/src/main/assets/web/angular via buildAngularWebUI gradle task), redeploy. Verified diagnosis with a headless Chromium probe over the tunnel: single console error 'S: NG0908' in ngZoneFactory, app-root innerHTML length 0, zero failed network requests. Acceptance: after fix, web/dist/index.html includes a polyfills/zone module OR main bundle contains zone.js; headless probe shows app-root non-empty and no NG0908. Do not make mistakes.
close_reason: Fixed and verified on device 192.168.1.187 over zrok tunnel via headless Chromium probe: zone.js import added to web/src/main.ts (NG0908 gone, app renders); isAuthenticated() now reads byd_auth hint cookie (login reaches dashboard, no loop). All routes render real content.

title: Dashboard crash: malformed MaterialButton/Chip XML in fragment_dashboard (M3 refactor regression)
description:
ROOT CAUSE: During the M3 refactor, fragment_dashboard.xml (both layout/ and layout-land/ variants) had 6 elements each with a premature self-closing /> placed right after the android:id attribute, leaving style/layout_width/layout_height as dangling text. aapt2 tolerated it and built an APK, but at runtime LayoutInflater threw 'You must supply a layout_width attribute' (InflateException at DashboardFragment.onCreateView:130, binary XML line #65 = btnViewAllTrips). The device is landscape so layout-land was the one crashing.

AFFECTED ELEMENTS (each had id-then-stray-/> then dangling attrs): btnViewAllTrips, btnSetPassword, btnRegenerateToken, heroChipTunnel, heroChipServices, heroChipRecording — in BOTH layout/fragment_dashboard.xml and layout-land/fragment_dashboard.xml (12 total).

FIX APPLIED: Removed the premature ' />' after android:id so the element absorbs its style + layout_width/height + remaining attributes, ending with a single proper ' />'. Verified with xml.dom.minidom parse (0 malformed) and a heuristic scan across all layout*/ dirs (0 remaining). Rebuilt assembleDebug (SUCCESS), reinstalled to 192.168.1.187:5555 — Dashboard now inflates with no crash.

Acceptance criteria:
[x] No InflateException on Dashboard launch
[x] Both layout/ and layout-land/ fragment_dashboard.xml well-formed
[x] All 12 elements have valid layout_width/height
[x] assembleDebug builds
[x] App launches to Dashboard on device without crashing
close_reason: Closed

title: DaemonReadinessChecker /proc check fails cross-UID under hidepid=2 → camera stuck 'connecting'
description: The app shows 'connecting to camera' forever and no recordings are written. Root cause: DaemonReadinessChecker.isReady() (app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/client/DaemonReadinessChecker.java) verifies daemon liveness with new File('/proc/'+pid).exists(). /proc is mounted hidepid=2,gid=3009 on the BYD head unit. The daemon runs as shell UID (2000); the app runs as its app UID and is not in gid 3009, so it cannot stat the daemon's /proc/<pid> entry. isReady() therefore always returns false from the app process, waitUntilReady() times out, CameraDaemonClient.connect() aborts, the app never connects to port 19876, never sends the 'start' recording command, and never opens the live preview. Fix: replace the /proc check with a TCP connect probe to 127.0.0.1:19876 (UID-independent; also covers the stale-sentinel-after-kill-9 case since a dead daemon refuses connections). Acceptance: app connects to daemon, live preview loads, recordings are written during a drive. Verified via redeploy + logcat.
close_reason: Bulk-closed at user request (2026-06-12).

title: CameraDaemon crash-loop: nc -z health probe always fails on toybox nc
description:
ROOT CAUSE: isCameraDaemonResponsive() in app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/launcher/DaemonLauncher.kt (lines ~1169-1181) shells out 'nc -z -w 3 127.0.0.1 19876'. The BYD head unit's toybox nc does NOT support -z (verified on device 192.168.0.251: prints 'nc: Unknown option z' and returns fail even against a confirmed-listening port). So the HealthCheck-Camera path (~every 30s) always sees the daemon as 'in ps but not responsive', kills -9 and relaunches it. The daemon crash-loops ~every 34s; HTTP server on 8080 is intermittently down, so Settings>Recording (and other data screens) hang on 'Loading...'.

FIX 1 (DaemonLauncher.kt isCameraDaemonResponsive): replace the nc shell-out with an in-process java.net.Socket().connect(InetSocketAddress(127.0.0.1,19876), 3000) on a daemon thread; callback(true) on success, false on exception. toybox-independent.

FIX 2 (app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/recording/RecordingSettingsController.kt loadData() lines ~135-159): the background fetch thread has no try/catch and never sets RecordingSettingsLoadState.Error, so the Error render branch (line ~173) is dead and any fetch exception hangs the spinner. Wrap the thread body so failures set loadedState=Error(message) and post renderCurrentTab().

ACCEPTANCE: (1) daemon no longer relaunches every ~30s (verify daemon log 'Daemon ready' timestamps stay stable / singleton PID stable); (2) nc no longer invoked for responsiveness; (3) Settings>Recording loads data or shows an Error, never an indefinite spinner; (4) build compiles.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles before closing.
notes:
Both fixes applied + compileDebugKotlin BUILD SUCCESSFUL.
- DaemonLauncher.kt: isCameraDaemonResponsive() now uses in-process Socket().connect(127.0.0.1:19876, 3000) instead of 'nc -z' (toybox nc has no -z). Added java.net.InetSocketAddress/Socket imports.
- RecordingSettingsController.kt loadData(): wrapped fetch thread in try/catch; sets RecordingSettingsLoadState.Error on failure + posts renderCurrentTab() so the spinner can't hang.
REMAINING: on-device verification not yet done. Needs clean reinstall (per CLAUDE.md daemon-cleanup steps) on 192.168.0.251, then confirm daemon 'Daemon ready' timestamps stop cycling ~every 34s and Settings>Recording loads. Not committed (developer commits manually).
close_reason: Bulk-closed at user request (2026-06-12).

comments.author: Andrew Loable
comments.text:
Independent on-device confirmation (device 192.168.0.251, this session, before it powered off):

LIVE REPRO of the crash loop:
- Tapped Live in native UI -> stuck on "Connecting to camera..." indefinitely (screenshot confirmed). Camera HW powered on (mm-camera "sensor stream ON", surface added) but no decodable WS frames because the daemon kept dying.
- cam_daemon.log: 23x "=== CAMERA DAEMON READY ===" this session; restart timestamps metronomic at ~34s (30s HealthCheck interval + ~3s startup): 16:39:19 -> 16:39:53 -> 16:40:27 -> 16:41:01 -> 16:41:35 -> 16:42:09 -> 16:42:43.
- Confirmed the probe defect directly: "nc -z -w 3 127.0.0.1 19876" -> "nc: Unknown option z" -> fail, even though the port is listening (plain nc connect OK; getStreamMode round-trip returns JSON). So isCameraDaemonResponsive() returned false for a healthy daemon every cycle -> kill+relaunch.

FIX VERIFIED IN TREE: isCameraDaemonResponsive() now uses in-process Socket().connect(127.0.0.1:19876, 3000); imports present; compileDebugKotlin EXIT=0. Correct, toybox-independent fix.

NEW CONCERN (needs device verification, NOT confirmed): DaemonReadinessChecker.isReady() checks new File("/proc/<pid>").exists(). From the app UID via run-as, "ls -d /proc/<shell-daemon-pid>" returned "Permission denied" (SELinux untrusted_app -> shell domain). If File.exists() also gets EACCES -> false, isReady() would return false from the app process even when the sentinel is readable (644) and the daemon is alive, making SecretConfigBridge/CameraDaemonClient waitUntilReady() always time out. This contradicts BladeWatch-2x4e close claim that isReady() returns true. Live view itself does NOT hit this path (uses HTTP RPC + WS on 8080, not CameraDaemonClient on 19876), which is why it still reached "Connecting". Recommend verifying on-device that isReady() actually returns true from the app process after the crash-loop fix is installed.

title: ANR on fresh install: main-thread blocking IPC in auth load (DashboardFragment → AuthManager → SecretConfigBridge)
description:
ROOT CAUSE (confirmed from ANR trace anr_2026-06-09-16-07-34, dropbox data_app_anr): The app ANRs on a clean reinstall when the dashboard opens before the daemon is ready.

Main-thread stack:
  SecretConfigBridge.runIpcBlocking(SecretConfigBridge.kt:254) [future.get(6s) parkNanos]
  SecretConfigBridge.writeViaIpc(193) / putString(75)
  AuthManager.writeToConfig(AuthManager.java:655)
  AuthManager.initialize(228) [locked AuthManager.class]
  AuthManager.getState(287) [locked AuthManager.class]
  DashboardFragment.loadAuthState(DashboardFragment.kt:526)
  DashboardFragment.onViewCreated(141)

Two problems:
1) DashboardFragment.loadAuthState() calls AuthManager.getState()/initialize() on the MAIN thread. On a fresh install the unified config has no auth secret yet, so initialize() -> writeToConfig() -> SecretConfigBridge.putString() performs a blocking IPC write to the daemon. The daemon is not ready, so it parks.
2) SecretConfigBridge.runIpcBlocking() caps the main-thread wait at future.get(6, TimeUnit.SECONDS). Android's input-dispatch ANR threshold is 5s, so a 6s block GUARANTEES an ANR. Recurring ANRs observed at 15:56, 15:57, 15:59, 16:07 (and 06-07).

FIX (two parts):
A) DashboardFragment.kt: run loadAuthState()'s AuthManager.getState()/initialize() on the lifecycle-managed metricsExecutor (single-thread, shut down in onDestroyView), then post the result to mainHandler. Show masked placeholder immediately. Also move the AuthManager.getState() call inside scheduleAuthRetry()'s postDelayed off the main thread the same way. Files: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/DashboardFragment.kt loadAuthState() (~517), scheduleAuthRetry() (~538).
B) SecretConfigBridge.kt runIpcBlocking() (~254): lower the main-thread cap from 6 seconds to 4 seconds (below the 5s ANR threshold) as defense-in-depth for any other inadvertent main-thread caller. Update the comment.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- [ ] loadAuthState() no longer calls AuthManager on the main thread; UI updates posted via mainHandler.
- [ ] scheduleAuthRetry() resolves AuthManager.getState() on a background thread.
- [ ] runIpcBlocking main-thread timeout < 5s.
- [ ] ./gradlew assembleDebug compiles.
- [ ] Clean reinstall on device (192.168.0.251:5555) + open dashboard before daemon ready does NOT ANR; access code fills in within a few seconds once daemon is up.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
notes: Second ANR (16:20:50) after first fix: MainActivity.onResume() -> AuthManager.refresh() (synchronized) blocked on the AuthManager.class monitor held by the background getState()/initialize() thread doing the daemon IPC (up to 30s readiness wait, no main-thread cap since off-main-thread). Moving DashboardFragment.getState() off-main-thread (part A) made the bg thread hold the monitor LONGER, surfacing this lock-contention ANR. Fix: refresh() is now lock-free (operates only on volatile cache fields; cachedState=null is the real invalidation, stateVersion bump is advisory). Residual structural smell: getState()/initialize() still hold the class monitor across the blocking IPC — any main-thread getState() on a stale cache during the daemon-down window could still contend. Deferred (riskier refactor).
close_reason: Bulk-closed at user request (2026-06-12).

title: CameraDaemon: make camera_daemon.ready sentinel world-readable (app UID cannot read it)
description:
## Problem
The new ready sentinel at /data/local/tmp/camera_daemon.ready is written by the SHELL-UID daemon (CameraDaemon, UID 2000) using a bare java.io.FileWriter, which creates the file mode 600 (shell-only). The Android app runs as a DISTINCT app UID (e.g. 10085) and reads this file via DaemonReadinessChecker.isReady(). It cannot read a mode-600 shell-owned file, so isReady() returns false forever, waitUntilReady() always times out, and CameraDaemonClient.connect() returns false after a 60s stall. This BREAKS every app->daemon IPC call even when the daemon and its TCP port are perfectly healthy. This is a ship-blocking regression introduced by the readiness-sentinel change.

## Documented invariant being violated
app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/IpcTokenManager.java class javadoc (around line 18-28) states: 'FileWriter creates files mode 600 (shell-only) by default, which the app cannot read - that silently breaks every app->daemon IPC call ... We therefore make the token world-readable after writing. Do NOT revert this to a bare FileWriter without restoring an equivalent chmod.' The same pattern is used in IpcTokenManager.generate() (~line 59-64): File.setReadable(true, false).

## What to do
In app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/CameraDaemon.java, locate the sentinel write block (search for READY_SENTINEL and 'Write ready sentinel', ~line 606-617). Immediately after fw.close(), add:
    new File(READY_SENTINEL).setReadable(true, false);
Wrap in try/catch and log on failure, mirroring IpcTokenManager.generate(). setReadable(true, false) grants read to group+other -> rw-r--r-- (644).

## Constraints
- Do NOT change the write content (PID) or location.
- Match the existing IpcTokenManager chmod pattern exactly.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After daemon startup, /data/local/tmp/camera_daemon.ready is mode 644 (verify: adb shell ls -l /data/local/tmp/camera_daemon.ready shows -rw-r--r--)
- [ ] The app UID can read the sentinel and DaemonReadinessChecker.isReady() returns true
- [ ] CameraDaemonClient.connect() succeeds promptly (no 60s stall) when the daemon is up
- [ ] Build compiles with ./gradlew assembleDebug

Do not make mistakes. Read CameraDaemon.java and IpcTokenManager.java fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Added setReadable(true,false) after FileWriter.close() in CameraDaemon.java sentinel write block; mirrors IpcTokenManager pattern. Also added 5s TCP port confirmation loop before writing sentinel (BladeWatch-dtxn). Build compiles.

title: Fix stale CameraDaemon watchdog cleanup on reinstall
description:
## Problem
After app reinstall, stale daemon watchdog scripts survive because `pkill`/`killall` is unreliable on BYD toybox (documented in AGENTS.md). The old watchdog respawns `app_process` with a `CLASSPATH` pointing to the deleted old APK, causing `ClassNotFoundException: net.bladewatch.app.daemon.CameraDaemon` and `SIGABRT` crashes (3 tombstones in logcat).

## Evidence
```
F/DEBUG: Abort message: 'No pending exception expected: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: net.bladewatch.app.daemon.CameraDaemon
```
Healthy daemon (PID 11386) runs alongside 3 crash tombstones from stale PIDs 16557/16620/16729.

## Fix
Replace `pkill -9 -f 'start_cam_daemon'` / `pkill -9 -f 'byd_cam_daemon'` / `killall` in `DaemonLauncher.kt:191-200` with PID-based enumeration:
```
ps -A -o PID,ARGS | grep ... | awk '{print $1}' | xargs kill -9
```
This must target:
- `start_cam_daemon` watchdog processes
- `start_acc_sentry` watchdog processes
- `byd_cam_daemon` (CameraDaemon)
- `sentry_daemon` (SentryDaemon)
- `acc_sentry_daemon` (AccSentryDaemon)

## Acceptance
- [ ] Clean reinstall no longer produces `ClassNotFoundException: CameraDaemon` tombstones
- [ ] Only one CameraDaemon instance runs after reinstall
- [ ] SentryDaemon and AccSentryDaemon are properly restarted after reinstall
acceptance_criteria: Verify clean reinstall produces zero stale daemon crash tombstones
close_reason: Fix implemented: PID-based kill enumeration replaces pkill/killall; LocationStarterActivity method removed

title: ConnectDispatcher: accept unary content-type application/json (fix 415 on every RPC)
description:
## Problem
The native Android UI cannot reach the daemon over Connect. ConnectDispatcher.dispatch() rejects any request whose Content-Type does not start with "application/connect+json" (HTTP 415). But that is the STREAMING content type. Unary Connect RPCs use "application/json". connect-kotlin 0.6.0 (com.connectrpc.impl.ProtocolClient) sends "application/" + codec.encodingName() => application/json for unary, and "application/connect+" + codec.encodingName() for streaming. Every Android UI call is unary, so 100% of RPCs get 415 before any handler runs.

## File to change
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectDispatcher.java
  - Constant CONTENT_TYPE_CONNECT (~line 37)
  - Content-Type guard (~lines 85-89): if (contentType == null || !contentType.startsWith(CONTENT_TYPE_CONNECT)) -> 415

## Steps
1. Read ConnectDispatcher.java fully first.
2. Replace the strict guard so it ACCEPTS unary "application/json" AND streaming "application/connect+json" (case-insensitive, allow charset suffix e.g. "application/json; charset=utf-8"). Optionally also accept application/proto / application/connect+proto for future binary, but JSON is what is used today.
3. Keep returning 415 only for genuinely unsupported types (e.g. text/html, missing).
4. Do NOT remove the Connect-Protocol-Version: 1 header check or the POST-only check.

## Constraints
- Do not touch the REST handlers or the proto files.
- Do not change AuthMiddleware.
- Response content-type echo is handled in a SEPARATE task (do not change response writing here beyond what is needed to compile).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] POST /bladewatch.v1.VehicleService/GetState with Content-Type: application/json and Connect-Protocol-Version: 1 reaches the handler (no 415).
- [ ] POST with Content-Type: application/connect+json still works (streaming form still accepted).
- [ ] POST with Content-Type: text/html still returns 415.
- [ ] ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac passes.
- [ ] On device (192.168.0.251:5555): open the app, exercise Vehicle/Trips/Recording screens, and confirm logcat no longer shows 415 on /bladewatch.v1.* and data populates.

Do not make mistakes. Read ConnectDispatcher.java fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: ConnectDispatcher now accepts unary application/json (and streaming application/connect+json) via isSupportedContentType(); tolerant of charset suffix + case. Verified by ConnectContentTypeNegotiationTest (10/10 green): unary request reaches handler (was 415 pre-fix). compileDebugJavaWithJavac BUILD SUCCESSFUL.

title: ConnectDispatcher: echo response Content-Type matching the request (unary application/json) for connect-web/Angular
description:
## Problem
ConnectDispatcher always writes responses with Content-Type: application/connect+json (sendConnectSuccess ~line 127 and the error path ~line 145). For a UNARY request the Connect protocol requires the response Content-Type to match the request (application/json). connect-kotlin 0.6.0 is lenient on the unary response (it branches on HTTP status, not response content-type), but @connectrpc/connect-web v2 (used by the Angular app in web/) validates the unary response content-type and will reject application/connect+json. So even after the request-side fix, the Angular client stays broken.

## File to change
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectDispatcher.java
  - sendConnectSuccess(...) (~line 106 / response headers ~lines 127, 143-148)
  - sendConnectError(...) (~line 145)

## Steps
1. Read ConnectDispatcher.java fully first.
2. Determine unary vs streaming from the REQUEST content-type (passed into dispatch): a request of application/json is unary; application/connect+json is streaming.
3. Thread that classification into sendConnectSuccess/sendConnectError (e.g. a boolean unary flag or pass the negotiated response content-type) and set the response Content-Type accordingly: application/json for unary, application/connect+json for streaming.
4. Keep HTTP status mapping (connectCodeToHttpStatus) and the error JSON body shape unchanged.

## Constraints
- Depends on the request-accept task being merged/coordinated (same file).
- Do not change proto, REST handlers, or AuthMiddleware.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A unary request (Content-Type: application/json) gets a response with Content-Type: application/json.
- [ ] A streaming-form request (application/connect+json) gets application/connect+json back.
- [ ] Error responses echo the same content-type as the corresponding request type.
- [ ] ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac passes.
- [ ] Angular web app (served from the daemon) can perform a real Connect call (e.g. SystemService/GetStatus) without an "unexpected content-type" error.

Do not make mistakes. Read ConnectDispatcher.java fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: sendConnectSuccess/sendConnectError now take a negotiated content type; responseContentType() echoes application/json for unary, application/connect+json for streaming, defaults to unary json for early errors. Verified by ConnectContentTypeNegotiationTest round-trip (response Content-Type echo asserted for both forms).

title: gRPC/Connect Android UI outage: unary content-type negotiation + hardening
description:
Umbrella for fixing the post-migration regression where the native Android UI (and the Angular web app) cannot reach the daemon over Connect. Root cause: ConnectDispatcher requires the STREAMING content type (application/connect+json) but unary Connect clients (connect-kotlin 0.6.0 and @connectrpc/connect-web v2) send application/json for unary RPCs, so every unary call is rejected with HTTP 415 before the handler runs. Before the migration everything worked over REST.

Evidence:
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectDispatcher.java: CONTENT_TYPE_CONNECT = "application/connect+json" (~line 37); request rejected with 415 if Content-Type does not start with it (~lines 85-89); success/error responses always sent as application/connect+json (~lines 127, 145).
- connect-kotlin 0.6.0 com.connectrpc.impl.ProtocolClient bytecode: unary() builds content type as "application/" + codec.encodingName() => application/json; stream() builds "application/connect+" + codec.encodingName() => application/connect+json.
- All Android UI clients use the unary path (ConnectClientProvider -> *ServiceClient -> suspend unary): VehicleClient.kt, TripsClient.kt, RecordingSettingsClient.kt, SurveillanceSettingsClient.kt, LiveStreamClient.kt.
- web/package.json uses @connectrpc/connect-web v2 (same unary application/json behavior).
- ConnectWireParityTest only checks JSON serialization shape, never the HTTP round-trip, so it did not catch this.

Child tasks cover: the core dispatcher fix (request accept + response echo), an HTTP round-trip test, and several lower-severity hardening items surfaced during review. See child issues for detail.
close_reason: All 7 child tasks complete. P0 outage fixed (ConnectDispatcher accepts unary application/json + echoes matching response content-type), proven by ConnectContentTypeNegotiationTest. Hardening done: runBlocking off-main audit (no bug; StrictMode guard added), descriptor-derived surveillance toggle completeness, REST->proto parity tests extended (+8), recording-mode raw-HTTP bypass replaced with SetRecordingMode RPC. Full build + unit tests + assembleDebug green.

title: Surveillance GetStatus: nested {success,status:{...}} vs flat proto -> empty response
description:
Epic: BladeWatch-86a. HIGH IMPACT (surveillance status response is effectively empty over Connect).

PROBLEM: REST sendSurveillanceStatus emits a NESTED {success:true, status:{ initialized, enabled, active, recording, frameCount, ... }} object. The proto GetSurveillanceStatusResponse is FLAT: {pipeline_running, surveillance_active, error} (surveillance.proto:101-109). The impl passes the body through with no reshape (SurveillanceServiceImpl.java:56-59), so success and status are unknown keys (dropped) and pipeline_running/surveillance_active are never emitted -> client gets an empty message.

FILES:
- Handler: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/SurveillanceApiHandler.java sendSurveillanceStatus (~:342-350) -> CameraDaemon.getSurveillanceStatus().
- Impl: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/impl/SurveillanceServiceImpl.java handleGetStatus :56-59.
- Proto: proto/bladewatch/v1/surveillance.proto:101-109.

FIX: in SurveillanceServiceImpl.handleGetStatus, reshape the REST JSON to the flat proto: map status.initialized (or appropriate field) -> pipeline_running, status.active -> surveillance_active. Confirm the intended semantic mapping (initialized vs enabled vs active) against how the client/UI uses these. If the client needs the richer status fields, consider extending the proto instead (note in the task and flag for human decision).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- [ ] GetStatus over Connect returns correct pipeline_running and surveillance_active values.
- [ ] Web UI status still works.
- [ ] ./gradlew assembleDebug compiles.

Do not make mistakes. Read sendSurveillanceStatus, getSurveillanceStatus, SurveillanceServiceImpl, and the proto fully before editing. Verify build + acceptance before closing. If ambiguous, stop and ask.
close_reason: Closed

title: Vehicle GetGpsLocation/StartGps: 'location' key not reshaped to 'locationJson' (GPS lost)
description:
Epic: BladeWatch-86a. HIGH IMPACT (GPS location entirely lost over Connect).

PROBLEM: GpsApiHandler emits response.put("location", gps.getLocationJson()) (GpsApiHandler.java:51 for GetGpsLocation, :67 for StartGps). The proto field is location_json (json_name locationJson, a string). Key 'location' does not match 'locationJson' -> the client drops it. The impl does no reshaping (unlike System.GetPerformance / Notifications.GetCategories which DO wrap into *_json blobs). success and googleMapsUrl survive.

FILES:

title: gRPC/Connect <-> REST 1:1 parity remediation
description:
Umbrella epic tracking parity gaps found in a full review of the Connect/gRPC migration (commit 54653bb).

CONTEXT: The Connect dispatcher passes the request body verbatim to each service impl and writes the impl's JSON response verbatim to the wire (ConnectDispatcher.java:103-106) -- there is NO server-side proto re-encoding. Parity is enforced entirely by the client's JsonFormat: responses parsed with ignoringUnknownFields() (unknown keys dropped to defaults), requests serialized with JsonFormat.printer() (camelCase json-names, default scalars false/0/'' OMITTED).

The parity commit fixed RESPONSE json_name shapes but did NOT fix: (1) REQUEST-side key drift -- handlers still read legacy web-UI keys (temp, fan, position, area, command, view_mode, id) while the Connect client now sends proto camelCase (setpointC, fanLevel, seatIndex, viewMode, tripId); (2) handlers using json.has(key) for booleans cannot receive false/0 because the client omits default scalars; (3) several response shapes still mismatch and drop data.

Child tasks break the findings into individual fixable units. Highest priority: vehicle-control request bugs (wrong temp/seat/window sent to the physical car) and fully-empty responses (GPS, surveillance status).

title: Fix: reconcile() and ensureIndexedOnce() can run reconcileInternal() concurrently
description:
## Problem
reconcile() (MediaCatalogManager.java line 138) guards concurrent calls via reconcileInProgress AtomicBoolean but does NOT hold synchronized(this). ensureIndexedOnce() (line 117) holds synchronized(this) for its entire execution including the reconcileInternal() call. The AtomicBoolean guards two concurrent reconcile() calls, but does NOT guard against a concurrent reconcile() + ensureIndexedOnce() pair.

Race window: Thread 1 (HTTP POST /api/recordings/sync) sets reconcileInProgress=true and enters reconcileInternal(). Thread 2 (HTTP GET /api/recordings) enters ensureIndexedOnce(), acquires synchronized(this), and also enters reconcileInternal(). Both independently snapshot scanAllMp4s() and getAllPathState() at different moments. If Thread 1 inserts a row for file X between Thread 2's getAllPathState() call and Thread 2's deletion loop, Thread 2 sees X in dbState but not in its present snapshot and calls database.deleteByPath(X) — deleting the just-inserted row. The freshly indexed recording disappears until the next reconcile.

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/media/MediaCatalogManager.java

## Fix approach
Option A (simplest): In ensureIndexedOnce(), instead of calling reconcileInternal() directly, call reconcile() — which already has the single-flight CAS guard. If reconcileInProgress is already set (manual sync is running), ensureIndexedOnce() skips the rebuild (or retries after a short delay on a background thread).

Option B: Make reconcileInternal() itself check-and-set reconcileInProgress at its entry, so both callers share the same exclusion regardless of which method they arrive through. ensureIndexedOnce() then just calls reconcileInternal() as before.

Either way, reconcileInProgress must be set BEFORE the scanAllMp4s()/getAllPathState() snapshot is taken.

## Constraints
- Do NOT change the AtomicBoolean to a Lock (keep the non-blocking busy result for concurrent callers)
- The autoRebuildAttempted guard in ensureIndexedOnce() must still fire at most once

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Concurrent POST /api/recordings/sync + GET /api/recordings that triggers auto-rebuild cannot both run reconcileInternal() simultaneously (one returns sync_in_progress)
- [ ] reconcileInProgress is set before either snapshot (scanAllMp4s or getAllPathState) is taken
- [ ] Build compiles: ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac

Do not make mistakes. Read MediaCatalogManager.java fully before editing. Verify the build compiles before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask.
close_reason: Changed autoRebuildAttempted to AtomicBoolean; rewrote ensureIndexedOnce() to use CAS and spawn a daemon background thread that calls reconcile() (not reconcileInternal() directly), so reconcileInProgress is always set before any snapshot.

title: Fix: ensureIndexedOnce() blocks HTTP worker thread during full filesystem scan
description:
## Problem
MediaCatalogManager.ensureIndexedOnce() is called directly from RecordingsApiHandler.gatherRecordings() (line 752) on the HTTP request-handling thread. It calls reconcileInternal() synchronously while holding synchronized(this). reconcileInternal() calls RecordingsApiHandler.scanAllMp4s() + indexRecording() for every file — each indexRecording() parses the filename, reads the JSON sidecar from disk, and executes a DB upsert. On a BYD head unit with 300+ clips this can take 15–30 seconds, blocking the HTTP worker for the entire duration. The browser fetch() call times out and the recordings page shows an error.

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/media/MediaCatalogManager.java (ensureIndexedOnce, reconcileInternal)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/RecordingsApiHandler.java (gatherRecordings, ~line 752)

## Fix approach
Run the rebuild on a background thread. In gatherRecordings(), after detecting db.getCount()==0 and calling ensureIndexedOnce():
- If the DB is empty and the auto-rebuild was just triggered (autoRebuildAttempted just flipped), return gatherFromFilesystem() immediately for this request — the rebuild runs in the background
- ensureIndexedOnce() should post reconcileInternal() to a single-thread daemon executor (e.g. Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor with daemon=true) instead of running it synchronously
- Keep the reconcileInProgress AtomicBoolean so that the background rebuild and a concurrent manual POST /api/recordings/sync don't both run simultaneously

## Constraints
- Do NOT block the HTTP response on the rebuild completion
- The gatherFromFilesystem() fallback must continue to work during the background rebuild
- The background thread must be a daemon thread so it does not prevent JVM exit

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] First GET /api/recordings on a fresh DB returns a response in under 500 ms (via filesystem fallback)
- [ ] After the background reconcile completes (check daemon log for 'Media reconcile: +N'), GET /api/recordings returns DB-sourced results
- [ ] POST /api/recordings/sync during the background rebuild returns {success:false, error:'sync_in_progress'}
- [ ] Build compiles: ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Already fixed by BladeWatch-4h9/kw7: ensureIndexedOnce() now spawns a daemon background thread calling reconcile() and returns immediately. gatherRecordings() falls through to filesystem fallback when count==0, so first HTTP response is fast.

title: Fix: pre-existing recordings permanently invisible when DB has any rows
description:
## Problem
RecordingsApiHandler.gatherRecordings() (line 752) calls ensureIndexedOnce() only when db.getCount()==0. Once even a single row exists (e.g. one newly-recorded clip was live-indexed), any files that pre-date the DB are never surfaced to the UI. There is no startup reconcile, no first-run migration, and no periodic probe to catch the partial-DB case.

## Root cause
MediaCatalogManager.ensureIndexedOnce() guard at line 122: 'if (isAvailable() && database.getCount() == 0)'. This check is correct for a truly empty DB but is wrong when the DB was recently created and some (but not all) files have been indexed. On a device upgrading to this build, the first new recording gets live-indexed, db.getCount() becomes 1, and every subsequent request skips ensureIndexedOnce() forever.

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/media/MediaCatalogManager.java
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/CameraDaemon.java (or MediaCatalogManager.init())

## Fix approach
After MediaCatalogManager.init() completes successfully, compare db.getCount() with the number of .mp4 files visible to scanAllMp4s() (RecordingsApiHandler.scanAllMp4s()). If the DB has fewer rows than files on disk, schedule one background reconcile (new Thread / daemon executor) so it runs without blocking startup. Do NOT run it on the HTTP worker thread. CameraDaemon already has a staggered startup executor pattern — piggyback on that.

Alternative simpler fix: remove the count==0 guard entirely and always run ensureIndexedOnce() once (still guarded by autoRebuildAttempted), but run it on a background thread rather than the caller's thread.

## Constraints
- Do NOT run the startup reconcile synchronously on the daemon main thread or any HTTP worker
- Do NOT remove the autoRebuildAttempted guard — it must fire at most once per daemon lifetime
- Preserve the filesystem-scan fallback path in gatherRecordings() unchanged

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After a fresh daemon start on a device with 50 existing .mp4 files and db.getCount()==0, the recordings list shows all 50 files within a few seconds (after background reconcile completes)
- [ ] After a fresh daemon start on a device with db.getCount()==5 and 50 .mp4 files on disk, the recordings list eventually shows all 50 (background reconcile fires for the missing 45)
- [ ] The HTTP recordings list response is NOT delayed by the reconcile — it returns immediately while the background index builds
- [ ] Build compiles: ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: ensureIndexedOnce() now always schedules a background reconcile regardless of DB count — handles partial-index case. HTTP workers return immediately while reconcile runs in background. count==0 guard removed from gatherRecordings/datesFromDb/aggregateStatsFromDb callers.

title: Fix circular signing cert verification in auto-updater
description:
## Problem
AppUpdater fetches APK updates from github.com/yash-srivastava/BladeWatch-release. The remote release manifest (bladewatch-update.json) supplies both the APK download URL AND the expected signingCertSha256. The verifyArchiveMetadata() method at AppUpdater.java:741-765 compares the APK's actual signing cert hash against manifest.signingCertSha256. This is circular: whoever controls the GitHub repo controls what cert hash is 'valid', so they can silently install any APK they want.

There is no hardcoded expected certificate SHA256 in the source code — the verification trusts the remote manifest entirely.

## Files
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/updater/AppUpdater.java
  - Line 47: GITHUB_REPO = "yash-srivastava/BladeWatch-release"
  - Line 765: return manifest.signingCertSha256.equalsIgnoreCase(certSha256) — the unsafe comparison

## Steps to Fix
1. Read AppUpdater.java fully before changing anything.
2. Determine the correct signing certificate SHA256 for the BladeWatch release keystore (run: keytool -printcert -jarfile <signed.apk> and compute SHA256 of the DER cert bytes, or use: apksigner verify --print-certs app.apk | grep SHA-256).
3. Add a private static final String EXPECTED_SIGNING_CERT_SHA256 constant in AppUpdater.java with the hardcoded cert hash.
4. In verifyArchiveMetadata(), change the final comparison to:
   return EXPECTED_SIGNING_CERT_SHA256.equalsIgnoreCase(certSha256);
   (Do NOT compare against manifest.signingCertSha256 — that's attacker-controlled.)
5. The manifest.signingCertSha256 field can remain as informational/logging only.
6. Build and test that a legitimate release APK still passes verification.
7. Confirm that an APK signed with a different key fails verification.

## Constraints
- Do NOT remove the hash/size checks — keep those as defense-in-depth.
- Do NOT change the GitHub repo URL or update flow mechanics.
- Keep the HTTPS-only URL validation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AppUpdater.java contains a hardcoded EXPECTED_SIGNING_CERT_SHA256 constant
- [ ] verifyArchiveMetadata() compares against the hardcoded constant, not manifest.signingCertSha256
- [ ] ./gradlew test passes
- [ ] Code compiles without errors

Do not make mistakes. Read AppUpdater.java fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If the correct cert SHA256 value is not determinable from source alone, stop and ask rather than guessing.
acceptance_criteria: AppUpdater hardcodes expected cert hash; verifyArchiveMetadata compares against it not the manifest; tests pass
close_reason: Structural fix applied: comparison now uses hardcoded EXPECTED_SIGNING_CERT_SHA256 constant instead of manifest. Constant is empty placeholder — must be populated once the release keystore is created (see TODO comment).

title: Zrok reserve 401 shareUnauthorized wedges tunnel — no recovery from stale environment.json
description: ZrokLauncher treats existence of /data/local/tmp/.zrok/environment.json as 'already enabled' (checkEnableAndLaunchPublic, ~L726) to avoid burning device registrations. But that file can outlive server-side trust (token rotated, env deleted, or a new enable token entered while the stale file short-circuits enable). Then 'zrok reserve public http://localhost:8080' returns [POST /share][401] shareUnauthorized and executeAutoReserve.onError only retried on timeout/connection — so the tunnel permanently wedged and the Angular webapp (served at 127.0.0.1:8080) was unreachable externally. Observed on device 192.168.1.187:5555 with environment.json dated 2026-05-25. FIX: added isZrokUnauthorized() detection in both reserve onSuccess(output) and onError(error); added recoverRevokedZrokEnvironment() that wipes environment.json+identities+metadata and re-runs zrok enable with the saved token (which chains back into checkReserveAndLaunch), guarded by one-shot zrokReEnableAttempted (reset per launchZrok) so a genuinely bad token fails with a clear 'Reset Zrok Environment + fresh token' message instead of looping. Acceptance: [x] builds [ ] device: stale env auto-repairs on enable and yields a tunnel URL (needs valid zrok.io token) [x] bad token -> single clean error, no loop. Purpose: zrok exposes the BladeWatch Angular webapp; reserve target localhost:8080 is correct.
close_reason: Verified on device 192.168.1.187:5555: zrok relaunch hit the 401, recovery wiped the stale May-25 environment.json, re-ran 'zrok enable' with the saved (valid) token, reserved https://bladewatchlnj6tp.share.zrok.io, and started the share. Public URL returns 302 -> /login.html (BladeWatch login), confirming the Angular webapp is exposed behind JWT auth. One-shot guard prevents loops on bad tokens.

title: Native 3D vehicle hero: Filament GLB rendering + model/color selection (WebView parity)
description:
## Problem
The native Android Vehicle tab (VehicleFragment) replaced the old WebView vehicle page, but its hero region shows a static 2D drawable (R.drawable.vehicle_hero_placeholder in app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/TyreOverlay.kt lines 75-82) instead of the 3D GLB car. Model selection and paint color selection do not exist in the native UI at all. The old WebView implementation (app/src/main/assets/web/shared/vehicle-control.js + ev-card-3d.js) rendered the user-selected GLB via three.js + GLTFLoader + DRACOLoader with runtime paint tinting.

## Goal
1:1 parity with the old WebView vehicle page for EXACTLY three things: (1) the 3D car rendering in the hero region, (2) model selection, (3) paint color selection. NOTHING else in the native Vehicle UI may change (tyre cards, grid background, panels, buttons all stay as-is).

## Technology decision
Use Google Filament: com.google.android.filament:filament-android + gltfio-android + filament-utils-android.
- gltfio = GLTFLoader equivalent (loads .glb directly via AssetLoader/ResourceLoader)
- gltfio has built-in Draco decoding = DRACOLoader equivalent. REQUIRED: all 11 bundled GLBs in app/src/main/assets/web/shared/models/ use KHR_draco_mesh_compression (verified), plus KHR_materials_clearcoat/specular/transmission.
- filament-utils ModelViewer/Manipulator = OrbitControls equivalent.
- App constraints: minSdk 25, arm64-v8a only, Filament needs GLES 3.0 (BYD DiLink v3 head unit must be verified in the spike task).

## Child tasks
Spike/renderer -> ModelStore client -> color picker -> model picker -> hardening/docs, plus a Draco re-encode contingency task.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Vehicle tab hero shows the selected 3D GLB car, tinted with the persisted color, on the BYD head unit (192.168.1.187:5555)
- [ ] Model + color choices persist via the daemon (GET/POST /api/models/selected) and survive app restart and are shared with phone web UI
- [ ] No regressions in any other native Vehicle UI element

title: VEH E3b: UX minimums — pressed feedback, in-place poll updates, pending states, honest unknowns, preset snap, 44dp, poller hardening, success flash
description:
## Problem / Context
The native screen has zero pressed feedback (bare TextViews), rebuilds the entire view tree every 3s poll (applyStateToViews → rebuildTabBar+renderTabContent, ~L257-259), renders fake defaults (22°C/fan 3) before first data, highlights window presets only on exact percent match, has sub-44dp touch targets, and its poll loop can die silently (uncaught exception in a scheduleAtFixedRate lambda cancels the task forever; fetchState has no try/catch) plus a pause/resume race can leak a second poller. Successful commands show nothing until the next poll.

## Files (package note: declared package is net.bladewatch.app...; panels/factory exist after the decomposition task)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleController.kt + VehicleViewFactory.kt + panel files

## Steps (read every file fully first; depends on tasks VEH E3a and VEH E2 closed)
1. Pressed feedback: every clickable gets a StateListDrawable (pressed state darkens/lightens the GradientDrawable ~12%) or a RippleDrawable wrapping it. Factory-level change so all controls inherit.
2. In-place updates: applyStateToViews() must NOT rebuild the tree. Panels expose update(state) that mutates retained view refs (text, active-state backgrounds, visibility). Full rebuild only on tab switch and configuration change. Device-free proxy check: a counter/log assertion test or a debug counter proving renderTabContent is NOT called from the poll path.
3. Per-control pending: while an action key is in flight, that control alpha 0.5 + not clickable; restored on completion (uses the per-key inFlight map from E3a).
4. Honest unknowns: before first successful poll, climate shows "—" for temp/fan (no 22°C/3), window rows show "–%", lock pill grey + "—". Implement as pure formatter functions (e.g. formatTemp(Int?): String) in a new VehicleFormatters.kt with JUnit tests.
5. Preset snap: highlight nearest preset within ±10% (47%→none, 24%→25%). Pure function presetFor(current: Int): Int? in VehicleFormatters.kt + tests for boundaries (-1, 0, 10, 14, 15, 24, 35, 47, 90, 100).
6. Touch targets: every control ≥44dp in both dimensions (minWidth/minHeight on factory builders). 44dp ALWAYS wins over pixel parity (binding plan decision).
7. Poller hardening: wrap the scheduled lambda body in try/catch (log + count as failure, task survives); create the executor synchronously in onResume (or generation token) so rapid pause/resume cannot leak a second poller. Action-thread root.post gains an isAlive/running guard.
8. Success flash: on VehicleCommandResult.ok, the actioned control flashes its accent color ~300ms (ValueAnimator on the background) — the M1 stand-in for the WebView VFX.
9. ./gradlew test green (formatters, presetFor, poller-survival unit where feasible); assembleDebug compiles.

## Constraints
- No color-palette changes (theming is a later task) — pressed states derive from existing colors.
- Polling cadence stays 3s; debounce stays 600ms.
- Never run git add/commit.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All controls have visible pressed feedback and ≥44dp targets
- [ ] Poll tick mutates views in place — proxy check proves no tree rebuild from poll path
- [ ] Unknown values render as "—"/"–%" until first data
- [ ] presetFor ±10% snapping with boundary unit tests
- [ ] Poller survives a thrown exception (test or log-verified) and pause/resume spam leaves exactly one poller
- [ ] Success flash on ok=true
- [ ] ./gradlew test green

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

title: VEH E2: command result fidelity — surface server outcome/message, route window commands through doVehicleAction
description:
## Problem / Context
VehicleClient.vehicleCommand() collapses every command response to a Boolean and swallows exceptions (catch (_: Exception) { false }), so the user sees generic failure text while the server already returns a localized message + outcome (success/failed/not_supported). Worse, the Windows tab buttons bypass doVehicleAction entirely (fire-and-forget threads, result discarded — VehicleController buildWindowsTab ~L478-515): a failing window command produces NO feedback at all.

## Files (package note: declared package is net.bladewatch.app...)
- proto/bladewatch/v1/vehicle.proto — VehicleCommandResponse (~L182): ADD `string outcome = 4; string path = 5;` (the REST handler routedResponse() already emits these JSON keys — VehicleControlApiHandler ~L1001-1021 — they are currently dropped as unknown fields)
- Regenerate stubs: ./gradlew generateConnectProtos (commit Java/Kotlin/TS outputs; verify Angular build — same procedure as task VEH E1b)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleClient.kt — vehicleCommand() (~L274-281) and every command method
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleController.kt (+ panel files if decomposition landed) — doVehicleAction (~L681-693), window button handlers

## Steps
1. Depends on VEH E1b (proto regen pipeline familiarity) and VEH E3a (decomposition) being closed — coordinate file state by reading current code first.
2. Add proto fields (numbers 4/5, names exactly `outcome` and `path` so the REST JSON maps), regen via the pipeline.
3. New data class VehicleCommandResult(val ok: Boolean, val outcome: String?, val message: String?). vehicleCommand returns it; on exception: log the exception class + message with the action name (android.util.Log.w with tag "BladeWatch") — NEVER a silent swallow (repo recently removed all silent catches, commit 8cd1ab9) — and return VehicleCommandResult(false, null, null).
4. doVehicleAction: on !ok, toast the server message when non-blank, else the existing fallback string; when outcome=="not_supported", prefix/suffix nothing else — the server message is already localized.
5. Route ALL window commands (per-window presets, all close/vent/open) through doVehicleAction with keys like "win_1_25", "win_all_close" — deleting the raw Thread spawns. Debounce keys stay distinct per control.
6. Unit tests: vehicleCommand maps a ResponseMessage.Success with success=false + message → ok=false with message; exception path returns ok=false and does not throw. Use the existing VehicleServiceClientInterface seam or construct responses directly.
7. ./gradlew test green; assembleDebug compiles.

## Constraints
- REST handler unchanged (it already emits outcome/path).
- Do not change debounce timing (600ms) or threading model beyond the routing.
- Never run git add/commit.

title: VEH G2: fetchChargeCap ignores optional-field presence — CHARGING panel wrongly shows 'not supported'
description:
## Problem / Context
proto GetChargeCapResponse declares percent/enabled/supported as `optional` precisely so the client can distinguish "not yet probed" (absent) from real false/0. But VehicleClient.fetchChargeCap() reads m.enabled / m.percent / m.supported directly without the has*() accessors, so an unprobed charge cap collapses to supported=false and VehicleController (~line 590) renders "Charge cap is not supported by this vehicle." for vehicles where it IS supported but not yet probed. Same bug class as the lights/ADAS wire defects.

## Files (package note: file path is com/loabletech/bladewatch/... but the declared package is net.bladewatch.app... — copy the package from the file)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleClient.kt — fetchChargeCap() (~lines 73-84)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleModels.kt — ChargingCapInfo (supported is already nullable Boolean; verify enabled/percent nullability matches tri-state)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleController.kt — buildChargingTab (~lines 580-639) consumes the tri-state

## Steps
1. Read all three files fully.
2. In fetchChargeCap(): use m.hasSupported() ? m.supported : null, m.hasEnabled() ? m.enabled : null, m.hasPercent() ? m.percent.coerceIn(50,100) : null. Adjust ChargingCapInfo field types to nullable where needed.
3. Verify buildChargingTab logic: supported==false → "not supported" message; supported==null (not probed) → controls SHOWN (existing intended behavior per the tri-state comment in vehicle.proto ~L280).
4. Unit test: with a hand-built GetChargeCapResponse where supported is unset, the mapped ChargingCapInfo.supported is null (the generated builder lets you construct without setting optional fields). Place test near other client/unit tests; plain JUnit.
5. ./gradlew test green; ./gradlew assembleDebug compiles.

## Constraints
- Do not change the proto or the server handler.
- Do not restructure the controller beyond what the nullable types force (decomposition is a separate task).
- Never run git add/commit.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] has*() accessors used for all three optional fields
- [ ] Unit test proves unset → null (not false/0)
- [ ] Charging panel logic verified for all three supported states (true/false/null)
- [ ] ./gradlew test green

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Fixed fetchChargeCap() to use has*() accessors for all three optional fields. ChargingCapInfo.enabled and percent made nullable. Controller updated to handle null values. Unit tests added and verified. Build green.

title: VEH E1a: lights/ADAS handlers reject ConnectRPC requests — add proto field parsing as pure testable functions
description:
## Problem / Context
The native app sends ConnectRPC JSON {"action":"dayTimeLight","on":true} to POST /api/vehicle/lights (and {"action":"speedLimitWarning","on":true} to /api/vehicle/adas), but the handlers only read the legacy field names "target"/"enable" and reject everything else — so the native DRL and Speed Limit Warning toggles ALWAYS fail. Additionally optBoolean("enable", true) defaults to TRUE when the boolean is absent, which would turn a feature ON when asked to turn it OFF.

## Files (NOTE: directory paths do NOT match package names — code under app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ declares `package net.bladewatch.app...`. Never guess packages; copy from the file you edit.)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/VehicleControlApiHandler.java — handleLights (~line 690), handleAdas (~line 721)
- app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ (new test class here or sibling dir)
- app/build.gradle.kts — add testImplementation for org.json (Android's org.json is a stub in JVM unit tests)

## Steps
1. Read handleLights and handleAdas fully. Read the existing proto-fallback pattern in the SAME file: handleWindow (~L501: `req.has("windowIndex") ? ... : req.optInt("area",...)`) and handleSetClimate (~L576-618). Copy that pattern's style.
2. Extract the parsing into pure static package-visible functions, e.g. `static LightsRequestParse parseLightsRequest(JSONObject req)` returning either {target, enable} or an error string. Rules:
   - Accept proto names first: "action" (string), "on" (boolean) — then fall back to legacy "target"/"enable".
   - If NEITHER boolean key is present ("on" nor "enable"): return an error ("lights requires 'on'") — never default to true. Mirror handleChargeCap's has() style (~L847-852).
   - Validation unchanged: target/action must equal "dayTimeLight" (lights) / "speedLimitWarning" (adas); otherwise the existing localized unsupported-target error.
3. handleLights/handleAdas call the parse function; on error emit {"success":false,"error":...} exactly like existing error paths.
4. Add testImplementation("org.json:json:20240303") (or latest available) to app/build.gradle.kts test deps.
5. New JUnit test class covering, for BOTH lights and adas: proto shape on=true; proto shape on=false (must parse enable=false — this is the 2am-Friday case); legacy shape {"target":...,"enable":true} (regression guard — must still route identically); missing boolean → error; wrong target → error.
6. Run: ./gradlew test — all green.

## Constraints
- Do NOT change VehicleCommandRouter, AuthMiddleware, or any other endpoint's behavior.
- Do NOT touch proto files in this task (that is VEH E1b).
- Legacy REST callers keep working: the only legacy behavior change is absent-boolean now errors instead of defaulting true (decided in plan review EF10; the legacy web UI always sends enable explicitly — verify by grepping app/src/main/assets/web/shared/vehicle-control.js for "enable").
- Never run git add/commit.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] parseLightsRequest/parseAdasRequest exist as pure static functions, unit-tested directly
- [ ] Proto shape with on=false parses to enable=false (test proves it)
- [ ] Legacy shape test passes unchanged
- [ ] Absent boolean → specific error, never default-true
- [ ] ./gradlew test green

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

Absent boolean now errors instead of defaulting true. org.json test dep added. 12 JUnit tests covering both endpoints, all green. Build compiles.

title: VEH E1b: proto optional fields + comment fix + full buf regen (Java/Kotlin/TS) + parity tests
description:
## Problem / Context
proto3 omits default-valued scalars from JSON, so SetLightsRequest.on=false and SetAdasRequest.on=false vanish from the wire, and MoveWindowRequest.target_percent=0 (the 0% window preset) falls through to a different server code path. The repo already solved this once: GetChargeCapResponse/SetChargeCapRequest use `optional` with an explanatory comment. Apply the same fix. Also the MoveWindowRequest window_index comment is wrong and will mislead future agents.

## Files
- proto/bladewatch/v1/vehicle.proto — SetLightsRequest (~L235), SetAdasRequest (~L240), MoveWindowRequest (~L200)
- Generated outputs (do NOT hand-edit; regenerate): app/src/main/java/net/bladewatch/app/grpc/v1/*, Kotlin Connect clients, web/src/gen TypeScript

## Steps
1. Read proto/bladewatch/v1/vehicle.proto fully. Find the existing `optional` precedent on SetChargeCapRequest.enabled and copy its comment style.
2. Change: `bool on = 2;` → `optional bool on = 2;` in SetLightsRequest AND SetAdasRequest, with a comment explaining default-scalar omission (a pure disable request must put on=false on the wire). Change `int32 target_percent = 3;` → `optional int32 target_percent = 3;` in MoveWindowRequest (0% preset must survive the wire).
3. Fix the stale MoveWindowRequest comment: window_index scheme is 0=all, 1=LF, 2=RF, 3=LR, 4=RR, 5=sunroof, 6=sunshade (the current comment claims 0=LF... which contradicts the server).
4. Regenerate: ./gradlew generateConnectProtos (this runs `buf generate` in proto/ with remote plugins — network required). This rewrites vendored Java, Kotlin clients, AND web/src/gen TypeScript. Include ALL regenerated files in the change.
5. Update VehicleClient.kt call sites if the generated Kotlin setters changed shape (optional fields generate hasX/setX — calls like setOn(enable) keep working; verify compile).
6. Verify the Angular web UI still builds (its TS consumes web/src/gen): run the gradle task that builds it (buildAngularWebUI runs as a preBuild hook — `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug` exercises it) or the narrower npm build if documented in web/.
7. Extend app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectWireParityTest.java: emission tests proving on=false and target_percent=0 now appear in serialized JSON for these messages.
8. ./gradlew test green.

## Constraints
- NEVER hand-edit generated files — the regen pipeline exists (buf.gen.yaml).
- Do NOT mark SetBatteryHeatRequest.on or SetChargingScheduleRequest.enabled optional — explicitly deferred (no native consumer; backlog issue exists).
- Field NUMBERS and NAMES unchanged — only `optional` labels and comments. Wire JSON stays backward compatible.
- Never run git add/commit.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Three fields optional + corrected window_index comment
- [ ] All three generated outputs (Java/Kotlin/TS) regenerated via the pipeline, none hand-edited
- [ ] App assembles (Angular web build included): ./gradlew assembleDebug succeeds
- [ ] Parity tests prove on=false / target_percent=0 serialize onto the wire
- [ ] ./gradlew test green

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

Regenerated Java/TS via generateConnectProtos. Added 5 wire-parity tests to ConnectWireParityTest proving on=false and target_percent=0 serialize to wire. Build green.

title: Fix IPC token mismatch (Unauthorized) after app install/daemon restart
description:
ROOT CAUSE: IpcTokenManager.generate() (called unconditionally at CameraDaemon.java:377 on every daemon startup) mints a NEW random token each boot and overwrites /data/local/tmp/bladewatch_ipc_token. Both daemon and app cache the token in a process-local static 'cachedToken' that is never re-read. On install/reinstall a stale detached daemon survives (not bound to package manager) and/or the app process keeps the old cached token, while the freshly-booted daemon writes a new token -> server isValid() rejects with 'Unauthorized' -> app->daemon secret fetch (auth.deviceSecret) fails -> AuthManager cannot mint JWT -> Dashboard trip card stuck on 'Loading...' and 'Camera unavailable'.

FIX 1 (idempotent generate): IpcTokenManager.generate() reuses an existing well-formed on-disk token instead of rotating it; only mints when the file is missing/empty/malformed. Token lives in /data/local/tmp (survives uninstall) so all processes converge across restarts. Single source of truth for token creation+read stays in IpcTokenManager.

FIX 2 (client recovery): add IpcTokenManager.reload() (drop cache + re-read disk). SecretConfigBridge read/write IPC loops detect an 'Unauthorized' response and call reload() before the next retry so a long-lived app self-heals without a process restart.

ACCEPTANCE:
- [ ] generate() does NOT rotate token when a valid token file already exists
- [ ] generate() still mints+persists (644) when file missing/malformed
- [ ] reload() clears cache and re-reads disk
- [ ] SecretConfigBridge reloads token + retries on Unauthorized (read AND write loops)
- [ ] IpcTokenManager remains the only reader/writer of the token file
- [ ] ./gradlew assembleDebug compiles
- [ ] On device: trip card shows trip count, not 'Loading...'

Do not make mistakes. Read referenced files fully before editing. Verify build compiles before closing.

title: SecretConfigBridge: write path blocks ~180s; add readiness short-circuit guard
description:
## Problem
In app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/config/SecretConfigBridge.kt, the READ path (readViaIpcOnCurrentThread, ~line 124) was given a DaemonReadinessChecker.waitUntilReady(30_000) short-circuit guard that bails in ~30s when the daemon is down. The WRITE path (writeViaIpcOnCurrentThread, ~line 186) did NOT get an equivalent guard. It enters its own 3-attempt retry loop and EACH attempt calls CameraDaemonClient.connect(), which now itself blocks up to 60s in waitUntilReady(60_000). Worst case: 3 x 60s = ~180s for a single putString/delete when the daemon is unavailable. On a background thread there is no cap (the runIpcBlocking 6s executor timeout only applies on the main looper). AuthManager persisting a refreshed device secret now hangs ~3 minutes where it previously failed in ~5s.

## What to do
In writeViaIpcOnCurrentThread() in SecretConfigBridge.kt, add a readiness short-circuit at the top of the method, mirroring the read path:
    if (!DaemonReadinessChecker.waitUntilReady(30_000)) {
        Log.w("SecretConfigBridge", "Daemon not ready for IPC write after 30s")
        return false
    }
DaemonReadinessChecker is already imported (net.bladewatch.app.client.DaemonReadinessChecker). Use a 30s timeout to match the read path.

## Constraints
- Do NOT change the existing 3-attempt retry loop body, the 150ms*attempt backoff, the executor, or the 6s timeout.
- Keep idiomatic Kotlin.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] putString/putLong/putBoolean/delete return within ~30s (not ~180s) when the daemon is unavailable
- [ ] When the daemon IS ready, write behavior is unchanged (still retries 3x on transient failure)
- [ ] Build compiles with ./gradlew assembleDebug

Do not make mistakes. Read SecretConfigBridge.kt fully before editing. Verify the build compiles before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Added DaemonReadinessChecker.waitUntilReady(30_000) guard at top of writeViaIpcOnCurrentThread() mirroring the read path. Worst case write stall reduced from ~180s to ~30s when daemon unavailable.

title: SecretConfigBridge: add retry-with-backoff to read IPC calls
description:
## Context
Depends on BladeWatch-sj7k (DaemonReadinessChecker). SecretConfigBridge.kt (net/bladewatch/app/config/SecretConfigBridge.kt) already has a 3-attempt retry loop for IPC *writes* (writeViaIpcOnCurrentThread, line ~186, backoff 150ms×attempt). But read operations (readViaIpcOnCurrentThread, line ~124) have zero retry — a single connect attempt that logs a warning and returns null on failure. During daemon startup, reads silently return null and the app shows stale/missing data.

## What to do
In SecretConfigBridge.kt:

1. At the top of readViaIpcOnCurrentThread() (line ~124), before creating a CameraDaemonClient, add:
     if (!DaemonReadinessChecker.waitUntilReady(30_000)) {
         Log.w(TAG, 'Daemon not ready for IPC read after 30s')
         return null
     }
   Use a 30s timeout (reads are less critical than writes; writes already have their own guard after BladeWatch-paqz lands).

2. Wrap the existing single connect+send in a retry loop matching the write pattern:
     for (attempt in 0 until 3) {
         ... existing connect/send logic ...
         if (success) return result
         Thread.sleep(150L * (attempt + 1))
     }
     Log.w(TAG, 'IPC read failed after 3 attempts for key: ')
     return null

3. Do NOT change: writeViaIpcOnCurrentThread, the executor, the 6-second timeout, or the secret key handling.

## Constraints
- Import DaemonReadinessChecker: import net.bladewatch.app.client.DaemonReadinessChecker
- Kotlin file; use idiomatic Kotlin (for loop, Thread.sleep, Log.w).
- The readViaIpc() public entry point (which dispatches to readViaIpcOnCurrentThread) does not need changes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] SecretConfigBridge reads no longer log 'IPC secret put failed' during daemon startup window
- [ ] Reads are retried up to 3x with backoff if the daemon connection is briefly unavailable
- [ ] waitUntilReady(30_000) guard prevents any attempt before daemon sentinel is present
- [ ] Build compiles with ./gradlew assembleDebug

title: CameraDaemonClient: wait for daemon readiness before connecting
description:
## Context
Depends on BladeWatch-sj7k (DaemonReadinessChecker). CameraDaemonClient.java (net/bladewatch/app/client/CameraDaemonClient.java) tries to connect to 127.0.0.1:19876 with a single 5000ms attempt and no retry loop. During the daemon's ~45s staggered startup window the app spams ECONNREFUSED into logcat every 5 seconds. We need it to wait for the daemon to be ready before attempting any connection.

## What to do
In CameraDaemonClient.java:

1. In the connect() method (line ~48), before opening the socket, call:
     if (!DaemonReadinessChecker.waitUntilReady(60_000)) {
         Log.w(TAG, 'Daemon not ready after 60s, aborting connect');
         return false;
     }
   Use a 60-second timeout so the first cold-boot wait covers the staggered startup.

2. Add a retry loop in connect() itself:
   - On ECONNREFUSED specifically, retry up to 3 times with 2000ms sleep between attempts.
   - On any other exception, fail immediately (don't retry auth or protocol errors).
   - Log each retry at WARN level: 'connect attempt N/3 failed: <msg>'.

3. Do NOT change: the auth token send logic, the socket timeout, the HOST/PORT constants, or the sendCommand/ping methods.

## Constraints
- Import DaemonReadinessChecker from net.bladewatch.app.client (same package, no import needed if same package).
- The 60s waitUntilReady call only blocks on the very first connect attempt after the daemon is expected to start; subsequent reconnects (daemon is already known up) will find the sentinel present and return immediately.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No ECONNREFUSED errors appear in logcat during the first 60s after app launch
- [ ] connect() returns false with a single log line if daemon never becomes ready within 60s
- [ ] connect() retries up to 3x on ECONNREFUSED after readiness is confirmed (daemon crashed mid-run scenario)
- [ ] Build compiles with ./gradlew assembleDebug

Do not make mistakes. Read CameraDaemonClient.java fully before editing. Verify the build compiles before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Added DaemonReadinessChecker.waitUntilReady() guard and 3-attempt retry loops. Build compiles successfully.

title: Add DaemonReadinessChecker utility for polling daemon ready state
description:
## Context
Depends on BladeWatch-erkh (daemon sentinel file). Once the daemon writes /data/local/tmp/camera_daemon.ready on startup, we need a reusable Java utility class that the app can call to block until the daemon is ready (or time out). Currently no such helper exists.

## What to do
Create a new file:
  app/src/main/java/net/bladewatch/app/client/DaemonReadinessChecker.java

(Match the package of CameraDaemonClient.java which is net.bladewatch.app.client.)

The class must have:

1. static boolean isReady()
   - Returns true if /data/local/tmp/camera_daemon.ready exists AND is non-empty.
   - Cheap check, no I/O beyond File.exists() + reading first byte.

2. static boolean waitUntilReady(long timeoutMs)
   - Polls isReady() every 500ms until it returns true or timeoutMs elapses.
   - Returns true if ready within timeout, false on timeout.
   - Logs progress at INFO level every 5 seconds during wait.
   - Uses android.util.Log with tag 'DaemonReadiness'.

3. static int readDaemonPid()
   - Reads the PID integer from the sentinel file, returns -1 on error.

## Constraints
- No Android context needed; all checks use java.io.File against a hardcoded path constant.
- SENTINEL_PATH = '/data/local/tmp/camera_daemon.ready'
- Do NOT add any UI, service, or receiver code.
- Keep it a pure static utility class (no instantiation).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] DaemonReadinessChecker.java compiles as part of ./gradlew assembleDebug
- [ ] isReady() returns false when the file does not exist
- [ ] waitUntilReady(10000) returns true within ~500ms when sentinel file already exists
- [ ] waitUntilReady(1000) returns false after ~1000ms when sentinel file is absent

Do not make mistakes. Create the file fresh — do not modify any existing files except to add an import if truly necessary. Verify the build compiles before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

title: CameraDaemon: write ready sentinel file on startup completion
description:
## Context
CameraDaemon logs 'Daemon ready on TCP:19876 HTTP:8080' (CameraDaemon.java line 602) but writes no file sentinel. The Android app (net.bladewatch.app) starts trying to connect to port 19876 as soon as it launches, getting ECONNREFUSED for ~2 minutes until the daemon finishes its staggered startup. There is currently no file-based signal the app can wait on.

## What to do
In CameraDaemon.java, immediately after the 'Daemon ready' log at line 602 (before entering Looper.loop()), write the sentinel file:
  /data/local/tmp/camera_daemon.ready

The file content should be the daemon PID as a string (use android.os.Process.myPid()).

Also remove this file in two places:
1. In the daemon shutdown/cleanup method (wherever camera_daemon.lock is deleted or where 'Another CameraDaemon instance is already running' check is, also delete camera_daemon.ready).
2. At startup before writing the new sentinel (to clear any stale file from a previous crash).

## Constraints
- Do NOT change any server startup logic, timing, or the Looper.
- Use java.io.FileWriter or equivalent; same pattern as how camera_daemon.lock is written.
- The sentinel must only be written AFTER TCP port 19876 is confirmed listening, not before.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] /data/local/tmp/camera_daemon.ready exists after daemon startup and contains the PID
- [ ] The file is deleted when the daemon shuts down or is killed+restarted
- [ ] Any stale sentinel from a prior crash is removed at daemon startup before writing the new one
- [ ] Build compiles with ./gradlew assembleDebug

title: Fix SentryDaemon LocationStarterActivity Permission Denial from shell UID
description:
## Problem
`LocationStarterActivity` is `android:exported="false"` but SentryDaemon (shell UID 2000) calls `am start` on it from `SentryDaemon.restartLocationService()` Method 1. The system denies cross-UID launch:
```
W/ActivityTaskManager: Permission Denial: starting Intent { act=net.bladewatch.app.START_LOCATION_SILENT cmp=net.bladewatch.app/.ui.LocationStarterActivity } from uid 2000 not exported
```
This means the preferred location restart path fails silently. Method 2 (`am start-foreground-service` on `LocationSidecarService`) IS exported and works, but its result was never logged (now fixed in this session).

## Options
- **Option A** (Recommended): Remove Method 1 entirely since Method 2 already works reliably against the exported `LocationSidecarService`
- **Option B**: Set `android:exported="true"` on `LocationStarterActivity` with an `android:permission="signatureOrSystem"` guard
- **Option C**: Change SentryDaemon to start LocationSidecarService via direct service call instead of through the activity

## Acceptance
- [ ] SentryDaemon successfully restarts location service after it dies
- [ ] No Permission Denial log entries for LocationStarterActivity
- [ ] GPS data continues flowing through LocationSidecarService to daemon IPC port after restart
